page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 7B13 processors using the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring an exact one-to-one ratio between virtual and physical compute units. System memory totals 128 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA extensions.

Benchmark testing demonstrates high compute capabilities across multi-core and specialized computational tasks. The instance achieved strong top-quartile results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core evaluations, as well as PassMark CPU, extended instructions, encryption, and physics benchmarks. Database operations in PassMark and cached memory operations also ranked in the top 25 percent. In contrast, uncached memory bandwidth, Geekbench multi-core workloads, Clang software compilation, static web serving, and Redis key-value operations performed in the mid-tier category.

Architectural tradeoffs center on storage and hardware acceleration. The instance does not bundle local NVMe or ephemeral SSD storage, requiring reliance on external networked persistent disks for file system needs. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are also absent, and the AMD core topology omits AVX-512 instruction support. However, dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores deliver consistent per-core execution without resource contention, yielding efficient CPU throughput relative to standard multi-tenant virtual machines.

Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-32 is suited for compute-intensive enterprise workloads that align with a balanced memory footprint. Typical deployment scenarios include distributed application backends, mid-sized relational database systems, multi-threaded data processing, static and dynamic web application clusters, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference.
